import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 74

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

open scoped Topology Real

namespace Erdos74

open Erdos74

universe u
variable {V : Type u}

/--
For a given subgraph `A`, this is the set of all numbers `k` such that `A` can be made
bipartite by deleting `k` edges.
-/
def SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite {G : SimpleGraph V} (A : G.Subgraph) : Set ℕ :=
  { (E.ncard) | (E : Set (Sym2 V)) (_ : E ⊆ A.edgeSet) (_ : IsBipartite (A.deleteEdges E).coe)}

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/--
The set of edge distances to a bipartite graph is always non-empty because deleting all edges
from a graph makes it bipartite.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite_nonempty {G : SimpleGraph V} (A : G.Subgraph) :
    SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite A |>.Nonempty := by
  dsimp only [edgeDistancesToBipartite,Set.nonempty_def]
  refine ⟨_, A.edgeSet, fun _ a ↦ a, ?_, rfl⟩
  use fun _ => 0
  simp

/--
The minimum number of edges that must be deleted from a subgraph `A` to make it bipartite.
-/
noncomputable def SimpleGraph.minEdgeDistToBipartite {G : SimpleGraph V} (A : G.Subgraph) : ℕ :=
  sInf <| SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite A

/--
For a graph `G` and a number `n`, this is the set of `minEdgeDistToBipartite A` for all
induced subgraphs `A` of `G` on `n` vertices.
-/
def SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { (SimpleGraph.minEdgeDistToBipartite A) |
    (A : Subgraph G) (_ : A.verts.ncard = n) (_ : A.verts.Finite) }

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/--
The set of minimum edge distances to bipartite for subgraphs of size `n` is bounded above.
A graph on `n` vertices has at most `n choose 2` edges, and deleting all of them
makes the graph bipartite, providing a straightforward upper bound.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite_bddAbove (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) :
    BddAbove (SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite G n) := by
  use n.choose 2
  simp only [upperBounds, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite,
    SimpleGraph.minEdgeDistToBipartite, SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite]
  intro m h
  replace ⟨A, ⟨hn, h_fin, h⟩⟩ := h
  rw [← h]
  have : A.edgeSet.ncard ≤ n.choose 2 := by
    rw [← hn]
    have := h_fin.fintype
    have := Fintype.ofFinite ↑A.coe.edgeSet
    convert (A.coe).card_edgeFinset_le_card_choose_two
    · rw [← Set.ncard_coe_finset A.coe.edgeFinset, coe_edgeFinset A.coe, ← Subgraph.image_coe_edgeSet_coe A]
      exact (Set.ncard_image_iff (Set.toFinite A.coe.edgeSet)).mpr <|
        Function.Injective.injOn <| Sym2.map.injective Subtype.coe_injective
    · rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card _ h_fin, Set.Finite.card_toFinset]
  refine le_trans ?_ this
  apply Nat.sInf_le
  simp only [Subgraph.deleteEdges_verts, exists_prop, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
  use A.edgeSet
  refine ⟨by rfl, ?_, rfl⟩
  use fun _ => 0
  simp

/--
For a given graph $G$ and size $n$, this defines the smallest number $k$
such that any subgraph of $G$ on $n$ vertices can be made bipartite by deleting
at most $k$ edges.

This value is optimal because it is the maximum of `minEdgeDistToBipartite` taken
over all $n$-vertex subgraphs. This means there exists at least one $n$-vertex
subgraph that requires exactly this many edge deletions.
This is Definition 3.1 in [EHS82].

[EHS82] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A. and Szemerédi, E.,
  *On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs* Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117-123.
-/
noncomputable def SimpleGraph.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) : ℕ := sSup <| SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite G n

/--
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ possibly very slowly.
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $f(n)$ edges?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_74 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop →
    (∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ f n) := by
  sorry

/--
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $\sqrt{n}$ edges?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_74.variants.sqrt : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ n, G.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite n ≤ (n : ℝ).sqrt := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the remaining statements/comments

end Erdos74

findings.description: The docstring describes actual numbers of deleted edges for an unrestricted subgraph A, but that interpretation requires A.edgeSet to be finite. If A.edgeSet is infinite, choosing E = A.edgeSet contributes 0 because E.ncard = 0. For example, an infinite star with the extra edge {1,2} contains a triangle, yet 0 belongs to this set. This is a documentation-domain issue: both conjectures use the helper only on explicitly finite subgraphs.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/74 concerns 'every finite subgraph on n vertices'. EHS82, Definition 3.1, p. 121, likewise counts deletions from vertex sets A with |A| = n. The helper's docstring at lines 37–38 omits this finite-domain qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the docstring with 'For a subgraph A with finitely many edges', and optionally document the junk-value behavior outside that domain. No change to either conjecture is necessary.

findings.description: The unqualified description as 'the minimum number of edges' is not valid on all inputs permitted by the signature. For the infinite star on ℕ with the extra edge {1,2}, the genuine minimum is 1, while this definition returns 0 because deleting the entire infinite edge set contributes ncard = 0. Both facts were checked in Lean. The source-level statements remain unaffected because they restrict A.verts to be finite.
findings.source_evidence: EHS82, Definition 3.1, p. 121 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-11.pdf), takes the deletion minimum on finite n-vertex graphs; https://www.erdosproblems.com/74 makes the same finiteness restriction. The docstring at line 57 describes arbitrary subgraphs without that qualification.
findings.suggested_fix: State that this is the minimum deletion number when A has finitely many edges. If a meaningful invariant on arbitrary infinite subgraphs is desired instead, require finite deletion witnesses and use a codomain that can represent the absence of a finite solution.

findings.description: The docstring says 'all induced subgraphs', but the comprehension includes all finite n-vertex subgraphs and has no A.IsInduced condition. The sets genuinely differ: for K₃ and n = 3, the Lean set contains 0 via the edgeless spanning subgraph, whereas the induced-only set does not. These examples were proved in Lean. Their suprema nevertheless agree, so neither conjecture is misformalized.
findings.source_evidence: EHS82, Definition 3.1, p. 121, maximizes over graphs induced on A ⊆ V with |A| = n. The webpage phrases the equivalent bound using 'every finite subgraph'. The file's lines 63–68 incorrectly describe the intermediate set as induced-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'induced subgraphs' in the docstring with 'finite subgraphs'. It may be helpful to note that taking the supremum gives the same value as restricting to induced subgraphs.

findings.description: The attainment claim at lines 107–109 needs a nonempty family of n-vertex subgraphs. The signature permits, for example, V = Fin 0 and n = 1. Then the family is empty and its natural supremum is 0, but no attaining subgraph exists. This boundary case was checked in Lean. The definition still correctly gives the least vacuous upper bound, and the infinite-chromatic graphs in both conjectures avoid this issue.
findings.source_evidence: EHS82, Definition 3.1, p. 121, indexes its maximum by A ⊆ V with |A| = n. The problem at https://www.erdosproblems.com/74 assumes infinite chromatic number, ensuring such finite vertex sets exist; the helper's docstring extends the attainment assertion to arbitrary G and n.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the attainment paragraph by the existence of an n-vertex subgraph, or by V being infinite. Document that the value is 0 when there are no n-vertex subgraphs.

status_issues.source_status: The current source marks the main problem 'DISPROVED (LEAN)' and attributes a negative answer to GPT-6 Astra. The page and Bloom's exposition were last edited 3 September 2026. The square-root variant is explicitly still open.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/74: 'This has been solved in the negative and the proof verified in Lean.' Its remarks attribute a negative answer for a sufficiently slowly growing f to GPT-6 Astra; the exposition notes that the formalization establishes a suitable unbounded function.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change Erdos74.erdos_74 to category research solved and answer(False). Leave Erdos74.erdos_74.variants.sqrt marked research open.

reformulations.difference: The Lean maximum ranges over arbitrary finite subgraphs, whereas EHS82 Definition 3.1 ranges over induced graphs on n-element vertex sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The minimum bipartizing deletion number cannot increase when edges are removed. Every finite subgraph A is contained in the induced subgraph on A.verts, with the same vertex count; conversely, every induced subgraph is included in the Lean family. Therefore the two suprema agree, including empty families. Proved as Review74.max_eq_induced_max in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source directly requires suitable edge deletions for every finite subgraph; Lean expresses this through a natural-valued minimum followed by a supremum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite A.verts, A.edgeSet and every E ⊆ A.edgeSet are finite. Successful deletion sets are nonempty, so the natural infimum is attained and is ≤ k exactly when a successful deletion set of size ≤ k exists. The subgraph-distance family is bounded by n.choose 2, so its supremum is ≤ k exactly when each member is. The full right-hand-side equivalence with the direct finite-deletion formulation was proved in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean bounds the real cast of the maximum deletion number rather than directly quantifying deletion sets of size at most √n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonnegative real threshold r, the natural maximum is ≤ r exactly when it is ≤ ⌊r⌋₊. Applying the finite-deletion equivalence with that natural threshold gives precisely the source condition. The full existential statement equivalence was proved in scratch.lean; the integer bound was also checked equivalent to Nat.sqrt n.
